Two updates on the Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 + DFlash2 Spark recipe, both of which humbled me a bit.

1. The new official NVFP4 checkpoint with BF16 lm_head dropped and I assumed it would be a free quality win. Wrong. It's 40% slower (42 to 25 tok/s) because the DFlash2 draft was tuned against the quantized head's logits. Swap the head, acceptance falls from 4.8 to 3.2. And quality didn't move at all, 66-67/80 GSM8K either way. The quantized head + FP32 ranking workaround from r0b0tlab beats the clean fix. Lesson: spec decode couples the draft to your target's exact numerics. I compared before testing all sides of it.

2. r0b0tlab also pointed out our published numbers undersell the recipe since random token benching is the drafter's worst case. He's right. Real code prompts hit accept lengths of 9.6-10 out of a max 10, pushing C1 from 42 to as high as 66 tok/s. Even 96K context tasks hold 41-47 tok/s. So 42 is the floor, not the ceiling.

Full data going in the repo.
